title: Micro-legend API and incremental tooltip hydration for high-cardinality time-series
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Our time-series canvas now frequently renders >40 series per viewport for some customers. The existing legend and HTML tooltip approach creates a large live DOM and expensive layout cycles, leading to janky interactions on low-powered devices and noisy screen-reader output for high-cardinality charts.

Goal: Design a lightweight, modular micro-legend component and an incremental tooltip hydration pipeline that: (1) reduces DOM & ARIA churn, (2) supports tokenized color palettes and theme tokens, (3) keeps keyboard & screen-reader accessibility first, and (4) enables progressive enhancement for streaming data.

Scope: This ticket covers the design artifacts, interaction patterns, accessibility spec, and performance acceptance criteria. Engineering tickets will follow for the runtime integration, worker offload, and feature flags.

Key constraints and principles:
- Minimal DOM footprint: prefer an aggregated legend DOM with selective per-series nodes created on demand.
- Progressive hydration: initial legend uses serialized summaries (canvas-friendly) and only hydrates per-series nodes on interaction or viewport focus.
- ARIA-first summaries: provide a concise, localized ARIA summary line (e.g., "Showing 48 series. Top 3 highlights: error-rate, latency-p50, throughput") that updates at a low cadence and is optimized for screen readers.
- Token-driven styling: map design tokens (color-surface-1, semantic-critical, token-accent-2) to a scalable palette; palette selection exposed via micro-legend API for Dedicated/Private theming.
- Low-motion and low-power fallbacks: respect reduced-motion; provide a compact non-animated tooltip mode and a static canvas-drawn mini-legend for ultra-low power devices.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Micro-legend surface (collapsed state): a single compact row summarizing counts and top signals. Render as canvas or single DOM element with aria-roledescription and live region.
2) Expanded view: lazy-create per-series rows when user expands or tabs into the legend. Rows include a color swatch (CSS variable linked to token), short label, and optional micro-spark/sparkline thumbnail (SVG/canvas).
3) Tooltip hydration pipeline: tooltips begin as lightweight serialized payloads (title, small excerpt) embedded in the chart's data model. When the user hovers/focuses, we hydrate full tooltip DOM via an off-main-thread worker that fetches cached aggregates and lightweight annotations; fallback to pre-rendered canvas snapshot if DOM creation is blocked.
4) Keyboard & SR interactions: arrow/space toggles legend expanded state; each per-series row is focusable once hydrated; pressing ? triggers the ARIA summary modal for sighted keyboard users.
5) Token mapping: define token set for legend elements: legend-bg, legend-border, legend-text-primary, legend-text-muted, swatch-size-small. Document mapping to color scales and accessible contrast ratios (WCAG AA for large text, 4.5:1 for labels where possible).

Performance acceptance criteria:
- Initial legend DOM nodes <= 8 on first paint for charts with >20 series (remaining series summarized).
- Time-to-first-interactive for legend <= 120ms on median mobile (simulated mid-tier device).
- Tooltip hydration latency <= 60ms after hover/focus in warmed cache scenario; fallback canvas snapshot update <= 40ms for cold path.
- Memory growth capped: incremental hydration should garbage-collect per-series nodes after 30s of inactivity unless pinned.

Accessibility acceptance criteria:
- Provide an aria-live polite summary that updates at most once every 3s and contains concise metadata (series count, top 3 metrics, active filters).
- Focus order preserved: chart -> legend summary -> expanded rows (hydrated) -> tooltip content.
- Valid keyboard nav documented and tested with VoiceOver and NVDA.

Deliverables:
- Figma screens: collapsed micro-legend, expanded legend (hydrated & pinned), tooltip skeletons, reduced-motion variants. (link below)
- Component API spec for designers/engineers: props, events, token keys, accessibility hooks, telemetry points.
- Prototype: interactive web prototype (canvas + minimal DOM) showing hydration flow and keyboard behavior.
- Eval checklist: perf benchmark harness instructions, accessibility testing script, e2e scenarios.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should auto-collapse be for accessibility (users with screen readers may prefer expanded lists)? Proposal: user preference + heuristics: expand if <8 series or if user has a persisted preference.
- Persistent state: should pinned rows remain hydrated across navigations? Engineering scoping needed for cross-route persistence.
- ARIA verbosity: condensed summaries are friendly for SR users but may lose fine-grained info; include an opt-in verbose summary toggle.

Next steps:
- 2026-01-27: Design walkthrough with ENG (Diego, Mina) and PM (Jules) — DONE (see comment).
- Build prototype (design+frontend) by 2026-02-07.
- Accessibility audit scheduled with SQA on 2026-02-18.
- Hand off to ENG for implementation spike (ENG-83401) after prototype sign-off.

Acceptance criteria (for ticket completion):
- Figma files updated and linked, prototype demonstrating hydration and keyboard SR flows, and design spec approved by ENG and PM.

comments: 2026-01-27 — Diego Morales: Reviewed the walkthrough. Engineering agrees to the hydration approach but requested clearer telemetry hooks (legend.hydrate.start / legend.hydrate.end) and a feature flag for canvas-first fallback. Filed ENG-83401 to capture implementation spike.

2026-01-29 — Mina Patel (Accessibility lead): Proposed that aria-live summary include a "last-updated" token to avoid SR confusion during streaming. Also recommends limiting summary updates when playback mode is active. Scheduling accessibility audit for 2026-02-18.

2026-02-02 — Jules Park (PM): Prioritized this for the next release window; asked to add usage metrics we can expose in Console (legend hydration counts, per-chart hydration latency). Added PM-412 as a dependency.

2026-02-04 — UX Research: Quick intercept testing with 6 participants showed preference for collapsed summary on dense charts; users asked for an ability to pin 3 series to keep hydration immediate. We will include pin affordance in the prototype.

2026-02-05 — Diego Morales: Prototype branch opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charting-protos/pull/172. Frontend lead notes worker-to-main handshake pattern implemented; next: perf testing on low-end device suite.
